metadata.title: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) off injury report for Week 3
metadata.description: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) is off of the injury report ahead of Week 3's matchup against the New England Patriots.
metadata.analysis: Thomas is now off of the injury report and should be a full go heading into a Week 3 matchup against the New England Patriots. He isn't expected to be a strong fantasy option for the foreseeable future, however.

metadata.title: Brian Thomas Jr. Continues Sluggish Start
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. was once again a non-factor in the offense on Sunday. He finished with three receptions for 40 yards in the season opener, and he registered the same stat line on Sunday. Thomas was targeted eight times in Week 2, which is an encouraging sign for fantasy managers. The 23-year-old hasn't been able to capture the same magic from his 2024 rookie campaign, when he finished with 1,282 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. Thomas is too talented to continue posting these kinds of games, but fantasy managers might want to treat him as a WR3 going forward.

metadata.title: Brian Thomas Jr. goes for 40 yards in Week 2
metadata.description: Brian Thomas Jr. caught three of his eight targets for 40 yards in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
metadata.analysis: Thomas seemed healthy after dealing with a shoulder injury in Week 1. He wound up finishing second on the Jags in all receiving categories while drawing an encouraging eight targets. Thomas is clearly behind Parker Washington in the pecking order, but he appears to be ahead of Jakobi Meyers, making him a solid WR3 in fantasy moving forward. He will face the Patriots in Week 3.

metadata.title: Brian Thomas - Quiet stat line in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: Thomas brought in three of eight targets for 40 yards in the Jaguars' 20-13 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Thomas' inefficient afternoon saw him mirror his same stat line from Week 1. The 2024 first-round pick's start to the new season has been somewhat worrisome considering he often underwhelmed in 2025 while playing in head coach Liam Coen's offense for the first time. Thomas should continue to see plenty of opportunity, but it remains to be seen how he'll fare against a second straight tough secondary in that of the Patriots during a Week 3  home matchup next Sunday.

metadata.title: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) cleared to play Sunday
metadata.description: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
metadata.analysis: Thomas suffered a shoulder injury during the team's season opener last week, but he was able to practice all week and won't miss any time because of it. He has been cleared to play on Sunday and should continue to contribute in his usual capacity for the Jaguars for the foreseeable future.

metadata.title: Brian Thomas Jr. Looking to Overcome Week 1 Shoulder Injury
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) was limited at practice all week but has no injury status heading into a Week 2 matchup with the Denver Broncos. The third-year pro will be looking to get more involved in the passing attack after just three catches for 40 yards in Week 1 against the Cleveland Browns. That production all came early in the game before his shoulder injury where he looked good to start the game. He was able to return late in the first half, but was vastly overshadowed by Parker Washington for most of the game. The Jaguars' passing attack was great against the Broncos last season in a 34-20 win, but BTJ was also overshadowed by Washington in that game, in which he had just two catches for 18 yards. Many fantasy managers are hoping he can return to his rookie-season form, but the more time that passes, the less likely it seems that will happen. For now, BTJ should be viewed as a risky flex option against the Broncos.

metadata.title: Brian Thomas - Cleared for Week 2 action
metadata.description: Thomas (shoulder) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Denver, Ryan O'Halloran of the Florida Times-Union reports.
metadata.analysis: The Jaguars listed Thomas as a limited practice participant all week, after he played just eight snaps on offense after the first quarter of a Week 1 win over Cleveland. He did catch three passes for 40 yards in the opening quarter, and he likely would've played more if the Jaguars hadn't been up by three-plus scores for the entire second half. Still, there's some risk of re-injury, and continued risk of playing behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in multi-TE formations.

metadata.title: Brian Thomas Jr. Cleared to Play in Week 2
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) was limited in practice all week but does not carry an injury designation on Friday and is cleared to play in Week 2 on Sunday against the hosting Denver Broncos, according to Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union. Thomas returned from a shoulder injury in the Week 1 season-opening blowout win over the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, but he finished with only three catches for 40 yards while seeing both Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers find the end zone. There is bounce-back potential for the former first-rounder in 2026, but in Jacksonville's crowded WR room, Thomas is going to continue to be more of a WR4/flex option for fantasy managers, especially coming off a shoulder injury last week. In a late-season game in 2025 in Denver, Thomas did not do much, catching two of three targets for only 18 yards in a 34-20 victory.

metadata.title: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) limited again Thursday
metadata.description: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The young wideout remains banged up, still limited at practice due to a shoulder injury that he suffered in the season opener. It looks more likely than not that he will play in Week 2, but in the off-chance that he's sidelined, Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers will both benefit from his absence.

metadata.title: Brian Thomas - Stays limited Thursday
metadata.description: Thomas (shoulder) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Thomas now has back-to-back capped sessions under his belt due to a shoulder injury to kick off Week 2 prep, which isn't unexpected after coach Liam Coen told Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com on Monday that the wide receiver would be limited in practice this week. Nevertheless, Thomas now has one more chance to get back to full Friday before the jaguars potentially tag him with a designation for Sunday's game at Denver.
